items.text: A To do card on Home lists anything you need to fill in yourself. Each one has a button that takes you straight there, and Later hides it until tomorrow.
Waiting on a refund: open any purchase and tick I returned this, waiting on the refund. Home reminds you until you tap It came, and an imported refund for the same amount clears it on its own.
Reminds you when a paycheck should have come in but is not logged, and when last month's income is only a guess.
Reminds you about bills past their due day that are not checked off, and car insurance due in the next 2 weeks.
Reminds you about people who owe you for over 2 weeks, and last month's leftover that still needs to go to savings.
Nudges you when nothing has been logged in 3 days, when your last bank import was over a week ago, and at the end of each month to compare balances with your bank.
Add to Calendar now also adds a monthly close out reminder on the 1st.
Months with five weeks now get five weeks of spending money. November is 300, not 260, so staying under every week never shows the month as over.
Refunds and returns. Tick Refund or return when you add one and it gives that money back to the week it lands in. Refunds show in green.
Bank imports now list money coming in too, unchecked. Check only the refunds. Paychecks and card payments stay out.
The real car insurance bill no longer counts twice. Use I paid the insurance bill on the Goals tab and it comes out of the insurance fund, not your budget.
Imports have an Insurance bill, paid from the fund choice, and you can tick the same box when editing an old insurance charge.
Past months with no paycheck logged are marked Estimate. Tap Set this month's income on Budget, Month to type what you really got, even 0.
This month counts your usual income until all your paychecks are logged, and a month with three paychecks counts all three.
Forgive button on IOUs people never paid back. Pick whether it comes out of this week's money or your savings. Delete it to undo.
Paying someone back now counts as your spending, with a box to turn it off if you already logged that purchase.
The Subscriptions budget now adds up your subscriptions in Recurring bills by itself. Add Prime there as a subscription and the total updates.
Purchases paid from savings now lower your saved this year total.
Bank imports catch more duplicates: the same amount within 3 days, or a bill you already checked off that month.
Switching between School and Summer no longer changes the income guess for older months.
A bill you added that already has payments cannot be removed by mistake, which would have pushed those payments into your weekly money.
If you go over your weekly money a bunch in one month, whatever you still owe at the end of the month gets paid from that month's savings. Your next month starts clean.
If you spent all your income and there is no savings to cover it, only the part that could not be covered carries into next month.
Budget, Month now has a Month result card: income, spent, saved or over your income, and how far over your weekly money went.
The Savings card warns you when weekly overspending is eating into this month's savings.
On by default. Turn it off in Budget and income, under Rollover, with Pay it off from month end savings.
You can now add your own monthly bills in Budget and income. Tap Add a bill at the bottom of Monthly bills and fixed costs.
Name it whatever you want, like Amazon Prime, and set the amount. It counts as a bill, not your weekly money.
Bills you add yourself can be renamed or removed.
Added this What's new page under More. It lists every update, new feature and fix, newest first.
A blue dot shows on the More tab and the What's new row when there is something you have not read yet.
The list loads fresh from GitHub each time you open it, so it is always current. Offline, it shows the last copy it saw.
Check for updates no longer flashes and throws you back to Home. It only reloads when there really is a new version.
If you already have the newest version, it just tells you so.
After an update and your PIN, you land back on Settings with a message saying it worked.

title: Cover a bad week with savings

items.text: When you blow way past your weekly money, a Cover with savings button shows on the Home spending card.
It fills in the amount needed to get back on track. You can change it. It comes out of this month's savings instead of your next weeks.
Covered money shows as a note on the card, and you can undo a cover.
If you go over your weekly money, next week starts with that much less. Example: spend 80 of 60, next week is 40.
A big overspend keeps carrying until it is paid back.
On by default. Turn it off in Budget and income, under Rollover.
Counting started the week of Nov 22, so older weeks do not count against you.
The gas card on Home shows the gas money you did not use going to savings at the end of the month.
Mom payback is now a strict 150 a month bill.
Whatever is left at the end of each month counts as saved, with a running total for the year.
Your weekly money is split into types like Food, Fun and going out, and Shopping, so you can see where it went.
Added a monthly gas tracker on Home with a Log a fill up button.
All non bill spending now shares one weekly limit of 60 instead of separate monthly amounts.
Weekly spending money is now the main number on Home.
When a paycheck falls short of the plan, the app offers fixes for future checks.
Removed Dad's payment from the budget. Old history stays.
Updated the monthly budget numbers without touching any saved data.
Automatic balances: logging a purchase updates the card or account it was on.
Spending trends, a paycheck planner, and a subscription review reminder.
Bill reminders you can add to your phone calendar.
Rollover of unspent weekly money, search, and receipt photos.
Full step by step setup.
Weekly and monthly reports you can share or export as a CSV.
Fixed parts of the screen overlapping and styles that were being blocked.
Moved Add into the bottom tab bar.
Number boxes keep focus when you move between them.
Pop up sheets work at large text sizes.
Settling IOUs and deleting things now asks you to confirm.
Settings stay put on the blank setup, and button text is readable in light mode.
Setup asks for your savings and card balances.
You can pay cards from savings.
Switched to a 6 digit PIN that unlocks as soon as you type the last digit.
The PIN is now optional.
Added quick setup and a stronger reminder to back up.
Text size slider and color themes.
Check for updates button, and the app now grabs new versions from the internet first.
Quick add, weekly and monthly budget views, history, recurring bills, and card warnings.
IOUs with partial payments, and savings goals including the insurance fund.
CSV and screenshot import with category rules.
Everything is encrypted on your phone, with auto lock, optional Face ID, and encrypted backups.
Can I afford this checker, monthly recap, and a Sunday review.
I'm not Mahi button for a blank setup anyone can use.
